extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, research-integrity professionals, and science journalists
extracted.subtask_description: A category/archive page on Retraction Watch that collects news items about retractions and integrity problems in the physical sciences, summarizing individual cases and common failure modes. Useful for tracking reasons papers are retracted and patterns of misconduct or error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious flaws in research methodology, numerical results, and interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Retraction notices citing “serious flaws in the research methodology, numerical results, and interpretation of findings.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication review can identify methodological problems, incorrect numerical analyses, or faulty interpretation that undermine a paper's conclusions and warrant retraction. Check methods, calculations, and whether conclusions follow from results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image duplication / identical plots representing different systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of “identical plots supposedly representing different chemical systems.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duplicate or recycled figures presented as representing distinct experiments are a clear sign of misrepresentation. Verify that images are unique to each claimed experiment and inspect metadata or raw files where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-citation manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where self-citations multiplied between manuscript submission and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for excessive or opportunistic self-citation intended to inflate metrics. Compare reference lists across versions and assess whether citations are substantively justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compromised peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases describing “compromised” peer review processes that contributed to problematic publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure peer-review integrity (no fabricated reviewers, undisclosed reviewer-author collusion). Compromised review can allow flawed or fraudulent work to be published and later retracted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental technical errors (e.g., chemical analyses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Retractions for “fundamental errors in chemical analyses” and other technical mistakes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical mistakes that invalidate results are grounds for correction or retraction. Reviewers and editors should scrutinize analytical methods and reproducibility claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data reuse and suspiciously similar image noise indicating manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers flagged for “data reuse and images showing suspiciously similar patterns of background noise, suggesting manipulation.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar background noise or reused image fragments across images purported to be different indicates potential manipulation; examine raw data and image acquisition details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly similar images labeled as different materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances where images “meant to be showing different materials” are nonetheless highly similar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that images labeled as representing different samples/events are genuinely distinct; similarity may imply fabrication or mislabeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism / 'tortured phrases' as red flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Work described as “crawling with ‘tortured phrases’ – possible signs of plagiarism.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unnatural or awkward phrasing that mirrors other texts (tortured phrases) can indicate plagiarism or poor automated rewriting. Use plagiarism detection and manual reading to confirm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadequate editorial independence / editor-author dominance
rubrics_metrics.description: Scenario where an editor authored the majority of a conference proceedings volume, prompting retraction of the entire volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest where editors have disproportionate authorship or control over content. Editorial roles should be separate from authorship decisions for impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate authorship and affiliation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases where authors requested removal or correction of institutional affiliations, and notices stating “the affiliation was given incorrectly.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affiliations must truthfully reflect institutional involvement; misreported affiliations are a integrity issue and should be verified by journals during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circular or assumption-based methodology (invalid experimental design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: a student’s calculations assumed the law they aimed to confirm, leading to a retraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure experimental designs do not presuppose the outcome. Methods must be capable of genuinely testing hypotheses without circular assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Raw-data / spectral irregularities indicating alteration (e.g., repeating NMR noise)
rubrics_metrics.description: NMR spectra with interrupted baselines and repeating noise, where “repeating noise is only possible if the spectra are altered [or] fake.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect raw spectra and noise characteristics; reproducible/random noise patterns should be random. Repeating noise patterns suggest editing or fabrication and require scrutiny of raw instrument outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of community/post-publication review (e.g., PubPeer) in detecting problems
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple cases where PubPeer or community flags uncovered widespread issues leading to retractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-publication peer review is a key detection mechanism; editors should engage with community concerns, investigate claims, and act on substantiated evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics gaming and fraudulent publishing practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Discussion of fraudulent publishing in math, particularly “metrics gaming,” with recommendations to detect and deal with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor for behaviors aimed at gaming citation or publication metrics (salami-slicing, citation rings). Implement policies and detection practices to discourage metric manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressions of concern and investigation when data provenance is unclear
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals issuing expressions of concern while investigating “origins and integrity of … data” in figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When provenance or integrity of data is unclear, journals should issue expressions of concern and conduct formal investigations before deciding on retraction or correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher/editorial policy failures and need for stronger pre-publication review
rubrics_metrics.description: A journal revised its policies on reviewing work after issuing its first retraction, highlighting policy weaknesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should maintain robust pre-publication review policies and quality controls to prevent flawed research from being published; policy review is needed after failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspicion of paper mills and implausibly prolific publication records
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns linking very large publication counts and patterns to possible paper mills (e.g., prolific authors with many retractions and flagged papers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unusually prolific authors or suspicious clusters of similar papers should trigger scrutiny for paper-mill involvement; check coauthor networks, text/image reuse, and submission patterns.
